claim: On December 28, 2018 Jeffrey Epstein wrote an account of being recognized. Bates EFTA01010127, Data Set 9 of the Department of Justice release, reads in full: "A friend of a friend skyped me becasue they wnated some advice. she said she was working on a sex trafficing movie. she said she met this really beuatiful girl that used to be a sex slave for a guy with a private island. she met this pilot /girl at buring man i asked her if she had ever met epstein, she said no she hadnt and i said yes you have. . she almost fainted". The email was sent ten years after Epstein's 2008 Florida conviction for procuring a person under 18 for prostitution and seven months before his federal arrest. It is his own written account of telling a stranger that the man she was describing was him. It is not a statement made under oath or entered in any proceeding, and it does not identify anyone else.

notes: Backstage. Circulating versions describe this as Epstein admitting to being a sex trafficker. He does not use the phrase and the record should not put it in his mouth; what he writes is that a filmmaker described a girl trafficked by a man with a private island, and that he told her she had already met the man. The document is quoted nearly whole because paraphrase is exactly where this one gets inflated, and because the misspellings are his and are part of how the corpus is authenticated. The copy at EFTA02607373 in Data Set 11 is the one usually screenshotted; it is not in the local mirror, which holds 100 Data Set 11 documents, so this rests on the Data Set 9 copies. Group A on the document.
